purpose: Decide what a bookkeeping practice sells as a fixed monthly subscription: which niche of small businesses it commits to, how each tier's scope is defined in countable units of recurring bookkeeping work rather than in hours, how the fee for that scope is derived from the practice's own measured cost-to-serve rather than a copied rate card, how the offer is positioned honestly against hourly bookkeeping and do-it-yourself software, and which prospects are qualified in, priced, deferred behind a separately scoped catch-up, or declined and referred before any engagement begins.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the practice sells recurring monthly bookkeeping and management reporting packages to small owner-managed businesses; revenue is a fixed monthly subscription per client tier, not hourly billing

the practice performs bookkeeping-side work only; attest engagements, tax return preparation, tax positions and representation, and legal interpretation are outside it and are referred to a licensed professional

every fee, band edge, effort estimate and capacity figure in this KB is a mechanism to be measured inside the practice, never a market rate; no external rate card, benchmark table or competitor price is assumed or asserted as fact

licensing, title-use, engagement-terms and data-protection obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; this KB names obligation classes and requires current rules to be verified locally with a qualified professional

the practice holds client bank, processor and payroll access and unfiled documents, so confidentiality and least-privilege access discipline apply from the first sales conversation, before anything is signed
the offer is designed and sold by the same small team that delivers it, so a tier that cannot be delivered as described is not a real tier
exclusions: the post-sale diagnostic review, the cleanup and catch-up project's own scoping and execution, chart-of-accounts and workflow standardization, and the repeatable monthly close checklist covering feeds, reconciliation, categorization review and reporting-packet production - owned by the client onboarding, cleanup and monthly close KB
accuracy controls inside the close and the escalation of individual judgment calls to the client or their CPA - owned by the same onboarding and close KB

clients-per-seat capacity math, repricing cadence and execution against the existing book, ongoing scope-creep control inside live accounts, retention, the monthly-review conversation, seasonal and at-risk client handling, firing a mis-fit client, and referral engines with CPAs and niche communities - owned by the subscription pricing, capacity and client retention KB

attest and audit engagements, reviews and compilations, tax return preparation, tax positions or planning, payroll or sales-tax filing positions, representation before any authority, and legal interpretation of contracts or entity structure
personalized financial, tax, legal, insurance or investment advice to a client or prospect; this KB is educational and operational only
invented market rates, benchmark fee tables, competitor price lists, industry margin figures or market-size claims presented as fact
accounting software configuration tutorials, ledger mechanics and bookkeeping instruction for owners
hiring, subcontracting and staffing decisions for the practice itself

competency_questions.question: What exactly does this practice sell as a monthly subscription, and how do I tell whether a given request is inside it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBSCRIPTION_OFFER_CHARTER names the buyer, the recurring body of work, the rhythm class and the explicit refusals, and TIER_EXCLUSION_LIST supplies the written not-included list in client language

competency_questions.question: Where does bookkeeping stop and licensed-professional territory begin, and what do I say when a prospect asks me to cross that line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSED_WORK_BOUNDARY classifies every service line as bookkeeping-side or licensed-side, names the obligation class rather than asserting a jurisdiction's rules, and supplies the refusal and referral sentence

competency_questions.question: What access to a client's financial systems does each tier require, how is it granted, and what will the practice never accept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_DATA_ACCESS_ETHICS states the per-tier access requirement, the least-privilege provisioning method and the prohibited practices, and ENGAGEMENT_ARTIFACT_GATE requires those terms in writing before the first month

competency_questions.question: Which niche should this practice serve, and how do I compare trades, e-commerce, restaurants and professional services without guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICHE_CANDIDATE_MAP defines candidates narrowly and scores them on fixed-fee viability attributes, NICHE_WORKLOAD_SIGNATURE supplies the month-shape evidence, and NICHE_COMMITMENT_DECISION states what commitment changes

competency_questions.question: Why does niching compound, what would prove it is compounding here, and what does concentration cost me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICHE_COMPOUNDING_MECHANISM names the compounding channels with an observable signal for each, and NICHE_COMMITMENT_DECISION states the concentration limit, the named shock exposures and the reversal conditions

competency_questions.question: Which countable facts about a prospect's books decide the tier they belong in?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_UNIT_DEFINITION lists each unit with a definition, a verification source and band edges, and TIER_LADDER_ARCHITECTURE maps those bands onto rungs that differ by a named body of work

competency_questions.question: How is a fixed monthly fee arrived at honestly without copying anyone's rate card, and how do I check the number after the first months?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIXED_FEE_MECHANISM derives the fee from effort estimate, cost floor, uncertainty premium and value context with per-deal verification, and OFFER_VALIDATION_LOOP compares measured effort against the estimate on a stated rhythm

competency_questions.question: What happens when a client outgrows the tier they bought, or asks for something outside it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIER_BOUNDARY_TRIGGERS defines the sustained, gameable-resistant triggers agreed at sale and ADDON_CATALOG supplies the priced destination for discrete out-of-tier requests, with the promote-to-rung signal stated

competency_questions.question: How do I answer a prospect who says an hourly bookkeeper is cheaper, or that their accounting software already does this?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HOURLY_MODEL_POSITIONING gives the structural comparison plus the cases where hourly genuinely wins, DIY_SOFTWARE_POSITIONING gives the automation limits and the honest do-it-yourself disqualification, and PROOF_ASSET_KIT supplies evidence containing no invented results

competency_questions.question: Before I quote anything, how do I decide whether this prospect is a fit for a fixed-fee subscription at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIT_QUALIFICATION_SCREEN states the six tests and the four outcomes with a recorded reason for every prospect, and BOOKS_CONDITION_TRIAGE assigns a condition band that decides whether a monthly fee may be quoted yet

competency_questions.question: When must I decline a prospect rather than sell to them, and how do I decline without leaving them stranded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DECLINE_AND_REFERRAL_RULE separates mandatory from discretionary declines, supplies the refusal sentence and referral destination class, and forbids converting a decline into a fear pitch

competency_questions.question: What selling behaviour will this practice not use, and what extra care does a frightened or unsophisticated owner get?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_SELLING_STANCE fixes the disclosure order, the prohibited tactics, the distress recognition signals and the no-upsell-under-distress rule, and BOOKS_CONDITION_TRIAGE keeps the catch-up conversation factual rather than alarming

competency_questions.question: What must be written down and agreed before the first subscription month starts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_DISCIPLINE_AT_SALE requires every request raised in the sale to be captured as included, add-on or referred, and ENGAGEMENT_ARTIFACT_GATE lists the required contents and enforces the binary no-artifact-no-start rule

competency_questions.question: How would I know the offer itself is wrong, and what evidence forces a re-cut of the tiers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFFER_VALIDATION_LOOP names the four evidence streams and the four review questions, and FIXED_FEE_MECHANISM and TIER_LADDER_ARCHITECTURE state what is re-derived when the evidence says the rung is wrong

glossary.definition: A recurring monthly package whose price is fixed and whose content is a defined body of bookkeeping work, sold as a repeatable product rather than as an open-ended engagement billed by time.

A countable, client-verifiable fact about a set of books - reconciled accounts and feeds, a monthly transaction volume band read from statements, entities, sales channels or locations, currencies, and judgment-heavy classes such as inventory or job costing - used to place a client on a tier.
The short ordered set of monthly packages plus a labelled custom path, where each rung is separated from its neighbour by a named body of work and a scope-unit band range rather than by an adjective.

The observed description of what one month of a given niche's bookkeeping consists of: how money arrives and leaves, how many accounts and feeds reconcile, how documents flow and how late, which transactions need judgment, how the peak season differs, and the exception that recurs every month.

The practice's own measured cost of delivering one rung for one month - labour at a rate the practice is willing to sustain plus the software, insurance and review overhead that rung consumes - derived from its own records, never from an external benchmark.

The deliberate addition to a fee that covers the part of a rung's workload signature that is still hypothesis rather than observation; it shrinks as pilot months and served clients turn assumptions into measurements.
Work outside the purchased rung that gets delivered anyway because saying yes was easier than routing it, so the fee stays the same while the cost-to-serve rises and the precedent hardens.

Bringing periods before the subscription starts into a closable state; it is separately scoped and separately priced at sale here, while its diagnosis and execution belong to the onboarding, cleanup and monthly close KB.

An audit, review or compilation issued with a practitioner's report, reserved to appropriately licensed professionals; it is named here as a boundary class the practice never performs or implies, with current rules to be verified in the practice's own jurisdiction.

Telling a prospect that this subscription is not what they need - because their need is a licensed professional, or because their volume genuinely suits software or hourly help - and referring them on, accepting the lost sale as the correct outcome.

nodes.definition: Fix in writing, before any price exists, what this practice actually sells every month: a defined body of recurring bookkeeping and management-reporting work, delivered on a stated rhythm, for one fixed monthly fee, to one identified kind of small business. The charter names the buyer it is built for - an owner-manager who wants to stop touching the books and wants to know what the month will cost, not a finance manager shopping for hours - and the recurring responsibility the subscription accepts: books that are kept current, accounts that are reconciled, and a report the owner receives on a known rhythm. It states the rhythm as a promise class (a working-day window after the client's inputs are complete) rather than as a fixed calendar date the practice cannot always control, and it states the three refusals that give the product its shape: no hourly billing, no unbounded scope, and no work reserved to a licensed professional. Every downstream decision in this KB - niche, scope units, rungs, fees, qualification, engagement terms - is a refinement of this charter, and any proposal that cannot be traced back to it is a bespoke project wearing a subscription label.

included: the buyer the offer is built for
the recurring body of work the fee covers
the delivery rhythm as a promise class
the three structural refusals
traceability of every proposal back to the charter
excluded: fee levels and band edges, derived later from measured cost-to-serve
the close procedure that delivers the promise
capacity planning and portfolio economics

pros.claim: A written charter turns a vague we do bookkeeping into a product that can be quoted, refused and repeated
pros.example: a prospect asking for weekly cash-flow forecasting is recognized immediately as outside the recurring promise instead of being absorbed as a favour in month two

cons.claim: A charter written before a single client has been served encodes untested assumptions and can lock the practice into a promise it cannot keep
cons.example: committing to a reporting rhythm before learning how late a trades client's supplier statements actually arrive

failure_modes: writing the charter as marketing copy instead of as a scope commitment
letting each early deal quietly redefine what the subscription is
promising outcomes such as better decisions or lower tax instead of a defined body of bookkeeping work
acceptance_tests: the charter names the buyer, the recurring body of work, the rhythm class and the three refusals, and a person outside the practice can use it to decide whether a named request is inside or outside the subscription
revisit_triggers: prospects repeatedly ask for something the charter does not describe
the practice is routinely delivering work the charter does not name

base.update_signal: the first cohort of sold subscriptions shows the practice routinely delivering work the charter does not name

nodes.definition: Draw the line between the work this subscription may promise and the work that belongs to a licensed professional, and build the sentences that hold that line under commercial pressure. Bookkeeping-side work records and classifies transactions, reconciles accounts to statements, maintains the ledger and produces management reports for the owner. Licensed-side work includes attest engagements issued with a practitioner's report, tax return preparation, tax positions and planning, representation before a tax authority, and legal interpretation of contracts or entity structure. The boundary is drawn as classes of obligation rather than as a list of statutes, because licensing rules, protected titles, who may sign or issue what, and what a non-licensed provider may claim about a client's numbers all differ by jurisdiction and change over time: the practice names the class, refuses on the class, and verifies current rules in its own jurisdiction with a qualified professional before publishing any claim or designation. The deliverable is a boundary card the seller can read aloud - what we do, what we never do, who we hand it to - plus a rule that every boundary-crossing request is logged, because the pattern shows where the offer is being misread.

included: classification of every service line as bookkeeping-side or licensed-side
title, designation and claim discipline in marketing and proposals
the refusal and referral sentence
logging boundary-crossing requests
the verify-locally obligation
excluded: asserting the specific licensing rules of any jurisdiction as settled fact
performing, reviewing or opining on tax work
advising on entity structure, deductions or tax position

pros.claim: Refusing on a stated class rather than case by case keeps the answer identical whoever asks and whatever the deal is worth
pros.example: answering the question about whether the owner should change entity type with the same referral sentence whether it comes from a prospect, a client or a referring CPA

cons.claim: A hard boundary loses deals to competitors who blur it, and prospects experience the refusal as unhelpfulness
cons.example: a restaurant owner who wanted one provider for both the books and the tax return taking the whole engagement elsewhere

failure_modes: drifting into tax advice while explaining why a transaction was categorized a certain way
marketing language that implies a professional designation or attest capability the practice does not hold
assuming rules learned in one jurisdiction apply in another
acceptance_tests: every service line in the offer is classified bookkeeping-side or licensed-side, and each licensed-side item has a written refusal sentence and a named referral destination class
no marketing, proposal or website text asserts a specific licensing rule, protected title or designation without verification in the practice's own jurisdiction
revisit_triggers: a prospect request lands ambiguously on the line more than once
regulator or professional-body guidance changes
the practice begins serving clients in a new jurisdiction

base.update_signal: regulator or professional-body guidance changes, or a local qualified professional flags a claim in the practice's marketing or proposals

nodes.definition: Decide, as part of the product rather than as an onboarding detail, exactly what access to a client's money systems each tier requires, how that access will be granted, and what the practice will never accept - because bookkeeping runs on the most sensitive data a small business holds: bank and card feeds, payment processor accounts, payroll registers, customer lists and unfiled documents. The access design states the least-privilege form of every connection the tier needs (an accountant-role invitation in the ledger, a read-only bank or processor feed, a document intake channel the client controls and can revoke) and rules out the convenient alternatives that owners will offer: shared owner passwords, credentials sent by message or email, personal file-sharing accounts, and work from an unmanaged personal device. It also fixes what confidentiality a prospect is owed before they buy, because a discovery conversation exposes the true state of their books whether or not they sign, and it fixes how sample material used in selling is de-identified. This belongs to offer design because access changes what a tier can promise and what a prospect must agree to before month one.

included: per-tier access requirement
least-privilege provisioning method per system
the prohibited-access list used in the sales conversation
confidentiality owed to a prospect who never signs
de-identification rule for sales samples
excluded: the onboarding runbook that provisions, tests and documents each connection
internal device and software administration policy
breach-notification duties, which are named as an obligation class to verify locally

pros.claim: Deciding access as part of the offer means the risky improvisation never has to happen under time pressure
pros.example: a prospect who offers their online banking login on the call is redirected to a read-only accountant invitation without hesitation or apology

cons.claim: Least-privilege access takes longer to set up and some owners read the refusal as bureaucracy from a small supplier
cons.example: an owner who wanted to hand over one password losing patience while three separate invitations are explained

failure_modes: accepting owner credentials to close or start faster
using a real client's identifiable statements or reports as a sales sample
discussing a prospect's disclosed mess with a referral partner without their permission
acceptance_tests: each tier states the systems it needs, the least-privilege provisioning method for each, and the prohibited alternatives, and the prohibited list is spoken in the sales conversation rather than buried
every sales sample is de-identified or synthetic and traces to no real client
revisit_triggers: a platform changes its accountant-access or permission model
an access near-miss or incident occurs
a new tier or add-on requires a system not covered by the access design

base.update_signal: an access incident or near miss, a platform access-model change, or a locally verified change in data-protection obligations

nodes.definition: Set the selling behaviour of the practice as an enforceable rule set rather than a matter of personal tone, because sales pressure is the mechanism that breaks every other discipline in this KB. Disclosure-first means the fee, what is included, what is excluded, what the client must do, and the fact that catch-up work is separate are all stated before any commitment is requested - never discovered later in the engagement artifact. No fear-selling means the practice does not use audit threat, penalty stories or manufactured urgency to move a decision, does not imply consequences it cannot substantiate, and does not speculate about what an authority might do, which would also cross the licensed-work boundary. Vulnerable-owner care means recognizing the buyer who is frightened or unable to judge what they are buying - a lender deadline, an authority notice, a partner dispute, a first business with no financial vocabulary, a language barrier - and responding by slowing the conversation down, writing the options in plain words, declining to offer a higher tier while distress is present, and pointing them to the right licensed professional when that is what they actually need.

included: the disclosure order in the sales conversation
prohibited persuasion tactics
distress and comprehension signals to watch for
the slow-down, write-it-plainly response
the no-upsell-under-distress rule
excluded: relationship management after the sale and the monthly-review conversation
marketing channel and campaign strategy
specific consumer-protection statutes, named as an obligation class to verify locally

pros.claim: A written stance survives the month when the pipeline is empty, which is exactly when the temptation to close on fear is strongest
pros.example: a seller with no deals that month still telling a panicking owner that their first call is a tax professional rather than a bookkeeping subscription

cons.claim: Disclosure-first raises objections early and loses deals a vaguer pitch would have closed
cons.example: stating plainly that the catch-up project is separate and separately priced, and watching a price-sensitive prospect withdraw on the call

failure_modes: using penalty or audit language to accelerate a decision
quoting the highest tier to a distressed owner precisely because they are not evaluating carefully
letting silence about exclusions do the persuading
acceptance_tests: the sales sequence states fee, inclusions, exclusions, client responsibilities and the separateness of catch-up before any commitment is requested
distress and comprehension signals have a written response, and no higher tier is offered while those signals are present
revisit_triggers: a won deal is traced back to an urgency claim
a client says they did not understand what they had bought

base.update_signal: a complaint, a misunderstood-scope conversation in the first months, or a win traceable to urgency pressure

nodes.definition: Enumerate the specific kinds of small business this practice could serve and compare them on the attributes that decide whether fixed-fee bookkeeping works there, instead of on which industry sounds appealing. Candidates are named narrowly enough to be operationally distinct - residential trades contractors, e-commerce sellers concentrated on one or two marketplaces, single-site restaurants, small professional-services firms - because a broad label hides the differences that decide everything downstream. Each candidate is compared on the transaction shape it generates (volume, repetition, number of channels), the source systems its money and documents live in, how predictable a month looks and how violent its seasonal swing is, whether its owners already buy bookkeeping or must first be convinced that they should, whether they congregate anywhere that a reputation can travel, how dense that population is within the practice's reach, and how strongly serving them pulls toward licensed-professional questions the practice must refuse. The output is a comparison sheet and a defensible short list with the observation behind every score, not a winner - the winner is chosen after the workload signature is built.

included: narrow candidate definitions
comparison attributes tied to fixed-fee viability
reachability and referral-density assessment
a short list with the observation behind each score
excluded: market sizing, growth rates or revenue projections presented as fact
building the referral engine and community presence
the final commitment decision

pros.claim: Comparing narrow candidates surfaces disqualifiers that a broad industry label conceals
pros.example: seeing that a single-site restaurant and a small multi-site group differ more in daily sales handling than two unrelated trades do

cons.claim: The comparison rests on impressions until the practice has actually served each candidate, so early scores are opinions with a scoring sheet around them
cons.example: rating e-commerce as high-volume-but-automated before meeting a seller whose fees, refunds and reserves all arrive inside one net payout

failure_modes: defining candidates so broadly that the comparison decides nothing
importing market-size or growth figures from a marketing article and treating them as facts
scoring on personal interest and calling it analysis
acceptance_tests: each candidate is defined narrowly enough that two people would classify the same prospect identically, and every attribute score names the observation or conversation behind it
revisit_triggers: a candidate's source systems or channel mix changes
the practice serves a client from a candidate that was never scored

base.update_signal: serving a client outside the scored candidates, or a candidate niche changing the platforms its money runs through

nodes.definition: Build, for each short-listed niche, a description of what one month of its bookkeeping actually consists of - the workload signature that every tier band and every fixed fee later rests on. The signature names drivers rather than a headline transaction count: how money arrives (card-present sales, marketplace payouts net of fees and reserves, progress billings and retainage, retainer deposits), how it leaves (supplier statements, subcontractor payments, fuel and materials, tip pools, a payroll run somebody else operates), how many accounts and feeds must reconcile, how documents reach the practice and how late they typically are, which transaction classes need a judgment call rather than a rule, and how the whole shape changes at the niche's seasonal peak. It also names the recurring exception - the thing that goes wrong in this niche every single month, such as a marketplace payout that nets sales, fees, refunds and reserve movements into one deposit, or a contractor buying materials on a personal card. A signature is written from observation - a pilot month, a walkthrough with an owner, a real file used with permission - and until it is observed, every element carries the label hypothesis so that nobody prices against a guess by accident.

included: money-in and money-out shapes
account, feed and document-flow drivers
judgment-heavy transaction classes
seasonal shape
the recurring monthly exception
observed-versus-hypothesis labelling
excluded: the reconciliation and close procedure itself
clients-per-seat capacity and utilization math
published industry benchmark hours quoted as fact

pros.claim: Naming the recurring exception before pricing is what makes a fixed fee survivable in that niche
pros.example: pricing an e-commerce rung already knowing that every payout must be decomposed into gross sales, marketplace fees, refunds and reserve movements

cons.claim: A signature built from one or two clients generalizes badly, because one niche can contain two completely different operating styles
cons.example: two restaurants of similar size where one runs an integrated point-of-sale and the other hands over a folder of paper tickets

failure_modes: accepting the owner's self-description of their volume as the signature
missing the seasonal peak because every walkthrough happened in a quiet month
leaving a hypothesis unlabelled until it hardens into a pricing assumption nobody remembers making
acceptance_tests: each short-listed niche has a signature naming money-in, money-out, feeds, document flow, judgment classes, seasonality and the recurring exception, with every element labelled observed or hypothesis
revisit_triggers: a source platform changes its payout, statement or export format
a served client's month contradicts the signature
the niche's peak season passes and reveals a shape the signature did not predict

base.update_signal: a pilot month or a served client's actual work record contradicting an element of the signature

nodes.definition: Explain, and then deliberately exploit, the mechanism by which serving one niche makes each additional client in it cheaper and faster to serve, so that the decision to niche rests on something checkable rather than on fashionable advice. The compounding runs through five concrete channels. A categorization ruleset and account structure built for the niche is reused rather than re-derived for each client. An exception library turns each oddity encountered once into a known answer applied in minutes. Shared vocabulary and a fixed question set shorten discovery, because the practice already knows what a job-costing contractor or a marketplace seller is about to describe. Band edges and effort estimates are calibrated across many similar clients instead of guessed once. And referral density means clients in one trade know each other, so a reputation accumulates inside a group instead of dissipating across unrelated industries. Each channel has an observable signal - repeat use of the same ruleset, falling discovery time, a shrinking share of first-month surprises, unprompted referrals from inside the niche - and the practice tracks the signals rather than asserting the benefit.

included: the five compounding channels
the observable signal for each channel
how compounding lowers measured cost-to-serve and shortens the sale
excluded: building and running the referral engine with CPAs and communities
the standardized chart of accounts artifact itself
profit or efficiency improvements stated as figures

pros.claim: A stated mechanism turns niching from a slogan into a claim the practice can verify or falsify with its own records
pros.example: checking whether the second and third contractor client really did take less discovery time than the first, rather than assuming they did

cons.claim: Compounding is slow and nearly invisible across the first clients, so it cannot justify the niche decision by itself
cons.example: the third restaurant still costing almost as much to serve as the first because each ran a different point-of-sale system

failure_modes: asserting compounding while still serving every client as a bespoke case
counting the reuse of a template as compounding when the underlying work did not actually shrink
using the promise of future compounding to justify underpricing the early clients
acceptance_tests: each compounding channel names a signal the practice can observe in its own records, and at least one artifact is evidenced in use across more than one client in the niche
revisit_triggers: a second client in the niche cannot reuse the first client's ruleset
discovery time stops falling across successive clients

base.update_signal: measured discovery time and ruleset reuse across successive clients in the same niche

nodes.definition: Choose the niche the practice will actually organize itself around, state what commitment changes in operational terms, and cap the concentration risk that commitment creates. Commitment is not a marketing claim: the offer language, the tier bands, the discovery question set, the proof assets and the referral effort all point at one niche, and work outside it is either declined or accepted knowingly as a labelled exception carrying no promise of the same efficiency or price. Because commitment concentrates the practice's income in one sector's fortunes and one set of platforms, the decision carries an explicit concentration limit - a share of the book beyond which the practice deliberately opens an adjacent niche - together with the named shocks it is now exposed to, such as a marketplace changing its payout reporting, a local construction slowdown, or a hospitality downturn that closes several clients in the same quarter. The decision also records what would reverse it, so that changing niche is a considered move with evidence behind it rather than a drift back into quoting whoever calls.

included: the commitment statement and the artifacts it changes
the exception rule for out-of-niche work
a concentration limit with an adjacency plan
named shock exposures
reversal conditions
excluded: exiting or firing individual live clients
sector forecasts presented as fact
campaign and channel execution for the chosen niche

pros.claim: One named niche makes every downstream decision easier and every discovery conversation shorter
pros.example: a discovery call with a contractor that opens on job costing and retainage instead of on a blank page of general questions

cons.claim: Concentration means a single sector shock or platform change hits a large share of the book in the same month
cons.example: a marketplace altering its payout report format and forcing rework across every e-commerce client at once

failure_modes: declaring a niche in the marketing while quoting anyone who calls
letting concentration grow past the stated limit without anyone noticing
abandoning the niche after one difficult client
acceptance_tests: the commitment names one niche, lists the artifacts that change because of it, sets a concentration limit with an adjacency plan, and states the conditions that would reverse it
revisit_triggers: concentration passes the stated limit
a named shock hits the chosen niche
labelled out-of-niche exceptions stop being exceptional

base.update_signal: the concentration share, the out-of-niche exception rate, or a sector or platform shock inside the chosen niche

nodes.definition: Define the small set of countable, client-verifiable units of bookkeeping work that decide which rung a client belongs on, so that tier placement is an observation both sides can check rather than a negotiation about how busy the owner feels. Workable units are things the client can evidence from documents they already hold: the number of accounts and feeds that must reconcile including bank, card, loan and payment-processor accounts, a monthly transaction volume band read from statements rather than from memory, the number of legal entities or separate sets of books, the number of sales channels or locations, currencies in use, whether payroll and sales-tax filings exist and who owns them, and the count of judgment-heavy classes present such as inventory, job costing, retainage, tips or owner draws mixed into business spending. Each unit needs a definition precise enough that two people counting the same prospect land on the same number, a named verification source, and band edges. Things that cannot be verified before the sale - how responsive an owner will be, how disorganized the paperwork is - are deliberately not scope units; they are qualification signals or condition ratings handled by other nodes, because pricing on an unverifiable unit is guessing with extra steps.

included: the countable unit list with definitions
a verification source per unit
band edges expressed as a mechanism
the rule excluding unverifiable units
excluded: hours, which are an input the client never actually buys
the internal effort model and clients-per-seat capacity
cleanup effort estimation for prior periods

pros.claim: Countable units make an uncomfortable conversation objective and reviewable
pros.example: showing an owner the statement pages that place them in the higher volume band instead of debating how busy their business feels

cons.claim: Counting units before access is granted means trusting client-supplied evidence, and owners under-report almost every time
cons.example: an owner who forgets the second card and the personal account they use for fuel and materials

failure_modes: choosing units the client cannot verify from their own documents
using hours as a unit and reintroducing the hourly model through the back door
letting the unit list grow until quoting needs a spreadsheet nobody can follow in a conversation
acceptance_tests: each unit has a written definition, a named verification source and band edges, and two people counting the same prospect independently place them on the same rung
revisit_triggers: prospects routinely land between bands
a niche platform change makes a unit impossible to count
a unit stops predicting delivery effort once clients are served

base.update_signal: independent re-counts disagreeing on rung placement, or served months showing a unit that does not predict effort

nodes.definition: Cut the ladder of monthly packages so that each rung differs from its neighbour by a stated body of work and a stated range of scope-unit bands, never by an adjective. A workable ladder is short - a small number of rungs plus a labelled custom path - and each rung answers four questions in writing: which recurring work is performed, what the client receives and on which rhythm, which scope-unit bands the rung covers, and what the client themselves must do for the rung to function. The rungs are cut where the work genuinely jumps - a second entity appearing, an added sales channel, inventory or job costing entering the picture, a payroll interface arriving - rather than at intervals invented to manufacture an upsell path, and the lowest rung is designed to be genuinely deliverable rather than as a loss leader the practice will come to resent. The labelled custom path is what keeps the ladder honest: a prospect who does not fit is quoted a clearly labelled custom engagement or declined, instead of being squeezed onto a rung that will not hold once delivery starts.

included: rung count and the work that separates each rung
the four questions every rung answers
scope-unit band mapping per rung
client responsibilities per rung
the labelled custom path
excluded: the fee level itself, derived separately from measured cost-to-serve
capacity and utilization planning per rung
the close procedure that delivers each rung

pros.claim: Rungs defined by work turn the sales conversation into a placement exercise instead of a haggle
pros.example: an owner reading the middle rung and recognizing their second entity and their extra sales channel in the band table

cons.claim: A short ladder always mis-serves someone at the edges, and every edge case creates pressure to invent another rung
cons.example: a professional-services firm with very low transaction volume but three entities fitting no rung cleanly

failure_modes: rungs separated by words such as basic and premium with no difference in the work performed
a lowest rung that cannot be delivered at its assumptions without resentment
inventing a bespoke rung to win one prospect and breaking the ladder for everyone after
acceptance_tests: each rung states its work, rhythm, scope-unit bands and client responsibilities, and any two adjacent rungs differ by at least one named body of work
no rung has been created for a single prospect without being labelled a custom engagement
revisit_triggers: prospects repeatedly fall between rungs
the lowest rung consistently overruns the effort its band assumed
the validation loop reports a rung whose work no longer matches its band

base.update_signal: placement data from sold deals showing prospects clustering between rungs, or delivered work not matching a rung's band

nodes.definition: Write, for every rung, the list of work that is deliberately not included, in the plain words a client would actually use to ask for it - because an unwritten exclusion is an argument waiting to happen in month three. The list covers the four families that genuinely arrive: licensed-professional work such as returns, tax positions, attest reports and representation; catch-up and cleanup of periods before the subscription begins; ad hoc analysis and one-off requests such as a lender package, a budget model, a cash forecast or chasing a customer for payment; and third-party administration the owner assumes is bookkeeping, such as filing registrations, operating the payroll run, handling collections, or answering correspondence from an authority. Every exclusion names where the work goes instead - an add-on with its own fee mechanism, a referral to a licensed professional, or a plain refusal - so that saying no is never the end of the sentence. The list is a sales asset rather than fine print: it is shown during the sale, because an exclusion first discovered inside the engagement artifact has already cost trust that the practice cannot buy back.

included: the four exclusion families in client language
a named destination for every exclusion
using exclusions inside the sale rather than after it
excluded: scope-creep management across live accounts over time
scoping and delivering the cleanup project itself
drafting the legal terms that carry the exclusions

pros.claim: An exclusion read before signing converts a future dispute into a priced option
pros.example: a lender package request answered with a pre-agreed add-on rather than an awkward negotiation in the week the lender wants it

cons.claim: A long exclusion list reads as defensive and can make a small buyer feel fenced in before the relationship starts
cons.example: a first-time owner reading two pages of what they do not get and losing confidence in what they do get

failure_modes: writing exclusions in accounting language the client cannot map to their own request
hiding the list until the engagement artifact
excluding work in writing and then performing it anyway to seem accommodating
acceptance_tests: every exclusion is written in the words a client would use, names its destination, and is shown in the sales conversation before commitment is requested
revisit_triggers: the same unlisted request arrives from more than one client
an excluded item is routinely performed anyway

base.update_signal: the register of out-of-scope requests, or delivery records showing excluded work being performed unpriced

nodes.definition: Agree at the sale, in writing, the objective events that move a client from one rung to the next, so that a later fee change is the execution of a rule the client already read rather than a surprise they experience as a penalty. Triggers are expressed in the same scope units the ladder is built from: a transaction volume band exceeded across a stated run of consecutive months rather than in a single spike, a new bank or processor account added, a second entity or location opened, a new sales channel switched on, inventory or job costing appearing, an additional currency in use. Each trigger states what happens when it fires - which rung the client moves to, what notice is given, and from which period the new fee applies. The design work here is choosing triggers that cannot be gamed by splitting accounts and that a seasonal business does not trip every peak, and pairing each with its opposite so a client whose volume falls sustainably can move down. This node owns the trigger definitions the subscription is sold with; the cadence, the conversation and portfolio-wide repricing across an existing book belong to the practice-economics KB.

included: trigger definitions in scope units
sustained-breach versus one-off spike rules
seasonal treatment
downward triggers
what happens when a trigger fires, agreed at sale
excluded: repricing cadence, scripts and portfolio-wide fee reviews
retention handling of a client unhappy about a move
discount policy

pros.claim: Pre-agreed triggers remove the single worst conversation in a subscription practice
pros.example: a contractor who added a crew and a new account moving up a rung under a rule they read and initialled at signing

cons.claim: Triggers written too tightly punish ordinary seasonal swings and manufacture churn risk
cons.example: a landscaping client tripping the volume band every summer and facing an upgrade they plainly do not need in winter

failure_modes: defining triggers on a single month's spike
writing triggers only for volume and none for complexity
letting triggers fire silently and never acting, so the ladder quietly decays
acceptance_tests: each trigger names its unit, its sustained-breach condition, its seasonal treatment and its consequence, and the full set is shown to the prospect before signing
revisit_triggers: a seasonal client trips a trigger in a way the design did not intend
clients grow in a dimension no trigger covers

base.update_signal: observed client growth patterns showing clients outgrowing rungs in dimensions no trigger covers

nodes.definition: Derive each rung's fee as the output of a stated mechanism the practice can defend and re-run, never as a number copied from a competitor page or an industry article. The mechanism has four inputs and one test. The first input is an effort estimate for the rung's scope, built from the niche workload signature and measured on the practice's own pilot months rather than assumed. The second is a cost floor: the practice's own labour at a rate it is willing to sustain, plus the software subscriptions, insurance, review time and support overhead that the rung consumes. The third is an uncertainty premium, sized by how much of the rung's signature is still hypothesis rather than observation, and shrinking as evidence accumulates. The fourth is value context - what the work is worth to this kind of owner and what their visible alternatives cost them - used to sanity-check the derived number, never to replace the cost side. The test is per-deal verification: the first months of every new client are compared against the effort estimate that priced them, and a rung whose estimate is repeatedly wrong is re-derived rather than quietly absorbed. No fee level, band edge or benchmark figure is asserted in this KB as a market fact; the practice measures its own numbers, and any external figure that enters the conversation is labelled as an unverified claim.

included: the four fee inputs as mechanisms
the uncertainty premium tied to unobserved signature elements
per-deal verification against the first months
labelling every external figure as unverified
excluded: stating any specific rate, fee level or benchmark table as fact
repricing cadence and increases across the existing book
the practice's own tax treatment of its revenue

pros.claim: A fee with a derivation can be defended, re-run and corrected, whereas a copied number can only be discounted
pros.example: answering price pushback by walking through the accounts, channels and judgment classes the rung actually carries

cons.claim: The mechanism only becomes trustworthy once real months have been measured, so early fees carry genuine estimation risk that the practice, not the client, absorbs
cons.example: a first marketplace-seller client whose payout decomposition took far longer every month than the estimate assumed

failure_modes: anchoring on a competitor's advertised price and reverse-engineering the scope to fit it
leaving review time, software and insurance out of the cost floor
quoting a rung whose signature is still mostly hypothesis with no uncertainty premium at all
acceptance_tests: each rung's fee traces to the four inputs, with the effort estimate marked observed or estimated, and every new client's first months are compared against that estimate
no external rate, benchmark or competitor figure appears anywhere in the offer material as an unlabelled fact
revisit_triggers: measured effort diverges from the estimate for consecutive months
the workload signature changes
software, insurance or review overhead changes materially

base.update_signal: measured delivery effort from sold clients compared against the effort estimate that priced their rung

nodes.definition: Build a small catalogue of separately scoped, separately priced pieces of work the practice will perform outside the monthly rungs, so that a reasonable request has somewhere to go other than silently into the subscription. The catalogue covers what recurs in the chosen niche: an additional entity's books, an extra sales channel or location, a lender or landlord reporting package, a historical clean-up handled as its own project, extra user seats or an additional approval step, a rush turnaround outside the normal rhythm, or a data extract for a third party. Each entry states its trigger, its scope, its own fee mechanism - one-off or a monthly increment derived exactly the way rung fees are derived - and how long it lasts before it lapses or renews. Two rules keep the catalogue honest: nothing is delivered before it is agreed in writing, and an add-on that most clients end up buying is a signal to redesign the rung rather than an annuity to keep selling separately. Licensed-professional work never enters the catalogue at any price; it is referred out.

included: the recurring add-on set for the niche
trigger, scope, fee mechanism and duration per entry
the agree-in-writing-before-delivery rule
the promote-to-rung signal
excluded: delivering the cleanup project itself
any licensed-professional work, which is referred rather than priced
long-run scope-creep management inside live accounts

pros.claim: A named add-on turns an awkward yes into an ordinary transaction that nobody resents
pros.example: a landlord asking for a reporting pack answered with an agreed one-off item instead of a weekend of unpaid work

cons.claim: A large catalogue makes the offer feel nickel-and-dimed and slows every sale down
cons.example: a prospect counting six possible extras and concluding that the advertised monthly fee is not the real cost

failure_modes: delivering the add-on first and invoicing later, or never
adding licensed-professional work to the catalogue because a client asked for it
keeping an add-on separate long after most clients need it, so the rung is understated by design
acceptance_tests: each add-on names its trigger, scope, fee mechanism and duration, contains no licensed-professional work, and is agreed in writing before any delivery
revisit_triggers: an add-on is requested by a majority of clients in the niche
an add-on is repeatedly delivered without written agreement

base.update_signal: the frequency with which each catalogue entry is requested across the client base

nodes.definition: Build the honest answer for the prospect who says an hourly bookkeeper would be cheaper, by explaining what actually differs between the two structures rather than by disparaging the alternative or inventing what a competitor charges. Three differences are substantive. An hourly arrangement leaves estimation risk with the client and makes their bill rise exactly in the months when their business is hardest, while a fixed fee moves that risk onto the practice and makes the cost predictable and budgetable. An hourly arrangement pays the provider for time spent, while a subscription pays the practice for the work being done, which is why standardization, automation and a clean chart of accounts are in the practice's own interest under this model. And an hourly meter makes a client hesitate before asking a question, while a defined subscription scope invites the questions that fall inside it. The position also concedes plainly where hourly genuinely wins - irregular or one-off work, and businesses whose volume is too small or too erratic to band - and sends those prospects toward hourly help. What this node produces is a truthful comparison the seller can make, not a script engineered to defeat every objection.

included: the structural differences stated as mechanisms
the cases where hourly genuinely fits better
how to answer the cheaper objection without disparagement
excluded: asserting competitor rates, prices or margins as fact
claiming a specific saving amount for the client
retention conversations with existing clients

pros.claim: Naming the risk transfer gives the prospect a reason for the fee that does not depend on comparing hourly rates at all
pros.example: an owner who has already lived through two surprise invoices recognizing predictability as the thing they are actually buying

cons.claim: The honest version concedes ground and loses purely price-driven buyers
cons.example: conceding that a very small and very regular set of books is genuinely cheaper hourly, and losing that prospect on the call

failure_modes: quoting an invented competitor hourly rate to make the comparison land
disparaging hourly bookkeepers instead of comparing the two structures
hiding the fact that a fixed fee costs more in a quiet month
acceptance_tests: the comparison rests only on stated structural differences with no invented competitor figures, and it names the cases where hourly is the better fit
revisit_triggers: the same price objection defeats the comparison repeatedly
the practice starts winning deals only on price

base.update_signal: win and loss notes showing which part of the comparison actually moved prospects

nodes.definition: Answer the prospect who believes their accounting software already does this, by being precise about what automation genuinely handles and what it does not, and by disqualifying honestly when the software really is enough. Feeds, rules and suggested categorizations do move transactions into a ledger, and pretending otherwise damages credibility with an owner who can see it working. What automation does not do is decide the ambiguous transactions, notice the one that never arrived, reconcile the ledger to an actual statement balance, keep the owner's personal spending out of the business books, produce a report that a human has reviewed and will stand behind, or tell the owner when something looks wrong before it matters. The position is therefore about review, exception handling and accountability rather than about data entry, and it is made concrete with the recurring exception from the niche workload signature - the marketplace payout automation books as one income line, the inter-account transfer it records as revenue, the owner's card that mixes groceries with materials. Honest disqualification is part of this node: an owner with very few monthly transactions, one account and no employees is often better served by their software plus an annual visit to a professional, and telling them so is the correct answer even though it loses the sale.

included: what feed automation does and does not do
review, exception handling and accountability as the product
the niche-specific automation failure as the concrete illustration
the honest do-it-yourself disqualification
excluded: software configuration, rule building and training
product comparisons or accuracy claims about any vendor stated as fact
teaching a prospect to do their own books

pros.claim: Showing the specific transaction automation gets wrong in this niche persuades far better than a general argument about accuracy
pros.example: walking a marketplace seller through a payout that automation posted as a single income line, hiding the fees, refunds and reserve inside it

cons.claim: Software improves continuously, so any specific weakness cited today can be closed tomorrow and dates the argument
cons.example: a platform rule update that starts handling exactly the payout case the pitch was built around

failure_modes: overstating how badly automation performs and losing credibility with a competent owner
arguing against software with the owners who genuinely should be using it alone
making unverifiable claims about a specific vendor product
acceptance_tests: the argument names concrete, current, checkable limitations drawn from the practice's own niche experience, and it identifies the prospect profile that should stay do-it-yourself
revisit_triggers: a platform releases automation that closes the cited gap
prospects report that the cited example no longer happens to them

base.update_signal: platform release notes or client reports showing the cited automation gap has been closed

nodes.definition: Assemble the small set of artifacts the practice shows a prospect to make an invisible monthly service concrete, built entirely from de-identified or synthetic material and containing no invented results. The kit typically holds a sample monthly reporting packet built on fabricated but realistic figures and clearly labelled as a sample, a one-page map of what happens across a month showing what the practice does and what the client must do, the scope-unit band table and the exclusion list themselves as sales artifacts, and references or testimonials given with explicit written permission and containing no client financial detail. Two rules govern the whole kit: nothing identifiable about a real client appears without their written permission, and no outcome claim appears that the practice cannot substantiate - no invented savings, no benchmark statistics, no implied guarantee about a tax, lending or valuation outcome. Because the kit is built for one niche it speaks directly to that owner and outperforms a generic brochure, and because it is built from the current ladder it must be revised whenever the rungs, the exclusions or the report format change.

included: a sample packet on labelled synthetic data
the month map showing both sides' responsibilities
band table and exclusion list as sales artifacts
permissioned references
the no-invented-results rule
excluded: producing the real client reporting packet each month
case studies containing real client figures without written permission
guarantees about tax, lending or valuation outcomes

pros.claim: A sample packet answers the question every prospect actually has, which is what will I receive for this fee
pros.example: an owner seeing the one-page summary they would get each month and immediately asking about a line on it instead of about the price

cons.claim: A credible kit takes real time to build and dates quickly as the offer changes
cons.example: a sample packet still showing a report format the practice retired two revisions of the ladder ago

failure_modes: using a real client's statements or reports as a sample
adding an invented improvement figure to make the sample land harder
letting the kit drift out of sync with the current rungs and exclusions
acceptance_tests: every asset is de-identified or synthetic and labelled as such, carries no unsubstantiated outcome claim, and matches the current tier ladder and exclusion list
revisit_triggers: the tier ladder or the reporting format changes
a reference client withdraws permission

base.update_signal: a change to the tier ladder, the reporting format, or a reference client's permission

nodes.definition: Run every prospect through the same short screen before any number is discussed, so that the decision to quote is deliberate rather than reflexive. The screen tests six things. Is the business inside the committed niche, or is it a knowingly labelled exception. What does the prospect actually want - recurring bookkeeping, or a tax return, or an audit, or one person to fix one mess - because only the first of those is this product. Can the scope units be counted from evidence the prospect can produce today. Do the systems a rung assumes actually exist, and will the owner grant least-privilege access to them. Will the owner do their own part: forwarding documents, answering categorization questions inside a reasonable window, and keeping business spending separable from personal spending. And do their expectations sit inside the licensed-work boundary, or are they buying a subscription hoping to receive tax advice through it. The screen ends in exactly one of four outcomes - quote a rung, quote a rung conditional on an agreed separate catch-up, quote a labelled custom engagement, or decline and refer - and the outcome and its reason are recorded for every prospect including the ones who never receive a proposal, because the pattern of declines is the most useful evidence the practice has about its own offer.

included: the six screen tests
the four permitted outcomes
recording outcome and reason for every prospect
routing to the custom path or to decline
excluded: the post-engagement diagnostic review of the books
credit checks or assessment of the owner's personal finances
the decision to keep or exit an already-live client

pros.claim: A fixed screen stops the practice quoting out of politeness and produces the decline pattern that improves the offer
pros.example: three declines in a row for the same missing point-of-sale integration revealing a rung assumption that no longer holds in that niche

cons.claim: Screening before quoting feels slow and can lose a prospect who wanted a number in the first minute
cons.example: an owner who called for a price hanging up when asked six questions before hearing one

failure_modes: skipping the screen because the prospect came from a trusted referral partner
treating enthusiasm or likeability as evidence of fit
quoting before establishing what the prospect actually wants to buy
acceptance_tests: every prospect has a recorded screen result with all six tests answered and exactly one of the four outcomes chosen, including prospects who never receive a proposal
revisit_triggers: declines cluster on a single test
a client who passed the screen turns out to be a mis-fit within the first months

base.update_signal: the distribution of screen outcomes and the first-month experience of clients who passed it

nodes.definition: Read the condition of a prospect's existing books well enough, at the sale, to know whether a monthly subscription can start at all and what the quote must assume - without performing the diagnostic review that belongs to onboarding and without doing unpaid work. The triage is deliberately shallow and asks for evidence rather than reassurance: when was the last period reconciled, does a closing balance agree to a statement for that period, are there uncategorized or suspense balances sitting in the ledger, do all the accounts the owner mentioned actually appear in the books, is there a prior-year set of accounts, and is another provider mid-way through work on the file. It classifies the prospect into a condition band - current, lightly behind, materially behind, or unknown because access or evidence was not provided - and every band carries a consequence: quote the rung normally, quote the rung with a stated and separately priced catch-up path, or decline to quote a monthly fee at all until a scoped catch-up is agreed. The rule this triage exists to enforce is that a monthly subscription never silently absorbs a catch-up project; the catch-up is scoped, priced and delivered as its own piece of work under the onboarding KB.

included: the shallow evidence questions
the four condition bands
the consequence attached to each band
the never-absorb-catch-up rule
handling the unknown band
excluded: the full diagnostic review, the cleanup plan and its execution
any opinion on whether prior filings or prior-year accounts were correct
correcting prior periods during the sales process

pros.claim: A condition band set before quoting protects the first months, which is exactly when a mispriced subscription does the most damage
pros.example: discovering that no account has been reconciled for several periods and quoting the rung only once a separate catch-up is agreed

cons.claim: A shallow read misses buried problems and will sometimes under-call the condition, while a deep read at sale stage is unpaid work the practice cannot afford to repeat
cons.example: books that look current until an unexplained suspense balance surfaces in the second month of the engagement

failure_modes: absorbing catch-up work into month one to win the deal
performing a full diagnostic for free during the sales process
quoting on the owner's assurance that everything is up to date
acceptance_tests: every quote records a condition band supported by named evidence, and any materially-behind or unknown band carries either an explicit separately-priced catch-up path or a decision not to quote a monthly fee yet
revisit_triggers: a client's condition proves materially worse than the band assumed
the triage questions stop discriminating between bands

base.update_signal: the gap between the sale-stage condition band and what the onboarding diagnostic actually finds

nodes.definition: State the conditions under which this practice will not sell, and the manner in which it says no. The mandatory declines are: the prospect's real need is licensed-professional work such as a return, an attest report, representation or a legal question; the prospect asks for a treatment of their transactions that the practice believes would misstate the books, however it is dressed up; the prospect will not grant least-privilege access or insists on handing over shared credentials; the prospect will not agree to a separately scoped catch-up when the condition band requires one; or the expectation cannot be met inside any rung and no honest custom scope exists. The discretionary declines are fit judgments - far outside the committed niche, an owner who will not participate in their own bookkeeping, an expectation of ongoing advice the practice does not give. Manner matters as much as rule: decline plainly and early, without disparaging the prospect or their situation, name the kind of professional they actually need, offer a referral where a genuine one exists, and never convert the decline into a fear pitch for a different package. Every decline is recorded with its reason, because those reasons are the cheapest evidence the practice will ever get.

included: mandatory and discretionary decline conditions
the refusal sentence and the referral destination class
recording every decline with its reason
the rule against converting a decline into a fear pitch
excluded: exiting or firing an existing client
guaranteeing or vetting any specific firm as a referral
supplying the advice the prospect was actually seeking

pros.claim: A decline given early with a named alternative protects the prospect and the practice's reputation at the same time
pros.example: telling an owner facing an authority notice that their first call is a licensed tax professional rather than a bookkeeping subscription

cons.claim: Declines cost immediate revenue and are hardest to hold exactly when the pipeline is thin
cons.example: passing on a well-funded prospect who wanted the books to support a treatment the practice would not stand behind

failure_modes: accepting a doubtful client while privately planning to fix the problem later
converting a decline into a fear-based pitch for a larger package
declining rudely and losing a future referral source in the niche
acceptance_tests: every mandatory decline condition has a written refusal sentence and a referral destination class, and each decline is recorded with its reason and date
revisit_triggers: one decline reason recurs often enough to be an offer-design signal
a referral destination proves unreliable or unavailable

base.update_signal: the pattern of recorded decline reasons, and any engagement that in hindsight should have been declined

nodes.definition: Control the moment when most scope damage in a bookkeeping subscription is actually done - the sales conversation, where a friendly yes creates an obligation nobody priced and nobody wrote down. The discipline has three parts. First, a phrase set that keeps the seller from improvising: every request is answered as in the rung, an add-on, or referred, and never as something we can probably sort out for you. Second, a capture rule: every request raised anywhere in the sale is written into the proposal under one of those three headings, so that nothing survives as a verbal understanding, and if it is not written then it was not sold. Third, a precedent rule: any concession made to win a particular deal is labelled a one-off, dated, and given a review point, because an unlabelled concession silently becomes the standard for every future client the moment the seller remembers having said yes. This node owns the sale-stage anchor only; managing drift across a live client relationship over the following months belongs to the practice-economics KB, which inherits whatever this node wrote down.

included: the three-way answer phrase set
the write-it-into-the-proposal capture rule
labelling and dating concessions
handing the written scope forward to delivery
excluded: ongoing scope-creep control in live accounts and the monthly-review conversation
renegotiating an existing client agreement
the delivery workflow itself

pros.claim: A three-way answer removes the improvisation that costs the practice the most money over a year
pros.example: a prospect asking for invoice chasing hearing in the same breath that it is not in the rung and is available as a named add-on

cons.claim: Rigid answers can feel unaccommodating and cost warmth in a relationship-driven small-business sale
cons.example: an owner expecting flexibility hearing three scoped answers in a row and reading the practice as inflexible

failure_modes: agreeing to a small extra in order to close and never recording it anywhere
letting a concession granted once become the unstated default for everyone
delivery discovering sales promises only when the first month begins
acceptance_tests: every request raised during the sale appears in the proposal categorized as included, add-on or referred, and every concession is labelled one-off with a date and a review point
revisit_triggers: delivery reports performing work that was never captured in the proposal
the same concession is granted to several clients in a row

base.update_signal: delivery records showing work performed in the first months that was never captured in the proposal

nodes.definition: Define what must exist in writing before the first subscription month may begin, and treat it as a gate rather than as paperwork. The artifact names the rung and its scope of work; the scope-unit counts that placed the client there and the evidence behind them; the exclusion list with the destination for each excluded item; the fee, the billing rhythm and the upgrade and downgrade triggers agreed in advance; the catch-up path and its separate price wherever the condition band required one; the access to be granted, how it will be provisioned and the confidentiality commitment that goes with it; the client's own responsibilities including document deadlines and keeping personal spending separable; the boundary statement that points licensed-professional questions elsewhere; and the terms for ending the engagement, including what data the client receives back, in what format and how quickly. Because the wording of engagement terms and any professional, consumer-protection or data-protection obligation attached to them varies by jurisdiction and changes over time, the practice has its template reviewed by a qualified professional locally and verifies current rules rather than trusting a template found online. The gate is binary: no artifact, no first month, no access accepted.

included: the required contents of the engagement artifact
the binary no-artifact-no-start gate
handoff of the written scope to onboarding
the local professional review and verification obligation
excluded: drafting legal terms or asserting what any jurisdiction requires
the onboarding runbook that executes after the gate
renewal, termination handling and win-back of live clients

pros.claim: One gate makes every earlier discipline real, because anything not written simply cannot pass through it
pros.example: an upgrade trigger that was discussed on a call but never written being caught the week before month one rather than a year later

cons.claim: The gate slows the start and an eager client can lose momentum between agreeing and beginning
cons.example: an owner ready to grant access on the same call being asked to wait for the written scope to be issued first

failure_modes: starting work on a verbal go-ahead because the client seemed keen
issuing an artifact that states the fee but omits exclusions, access terms or triggers
using a downloaded template without any local professional review
acceptance_tests: every listed element is present and specific before the first month starts, and the template has been reviewed by a qualified professional in the practice's own jurisdiction
no engagement begins and no client credential is accepted without the artifact in place
revisit_triggers: a scope dispute reveals a missing element
the tier ladder, the access model or a named obligation class changes

base.update_signal: a scope dispute, a change to the ladder or access model, or a professional review of the engagement template

nodes.definition: Close the loop between what the practice sold and what it actually delivered, on a scheduled rhythm, so that the offer is corrected by evidence instead of by accumulated frustration. The loop assembles four evidence streams: measured delivery effort per client compared against the effort estimate that priced their rung; the register of out-of-scope requests and which of the three destinations each was routed to; screen outcomes and recorded decline reasons; and win and loss notes naming the objection that decided each. From those it answers four questions: is any rung systematically underpriced or over-scoped, is any scope unit failing to predict effort, is the exclusion list missing a request that keeps arriving, and is the niche commitment still supported by the pipeline it is producing. Its outputs are changes to this KB's own artifacts - re-cut bands, re-derived fees, an add-on promoted into a rung, revised triggers, a re-scored niche - applied to new sales directly, and handed to the practice-economics KB whenever the change must be executed against clients who already bought. The loop is deliberately scheduled, because a small practice never feels it has time for it and the cost of skipping it only appears a year later.

included: the four evidence streams
the four review questions
changes to bands, fees, exclusions and triggers for new sales
handoff of existing-client changes to the practice-economics KB
excluded: executing repricing on the existing book and the conversations that requires
delivery quality controls inside the monthly close
presenting any of this evidence externally as market benchmark data

pros.claim: A scheduled loop catches a mispriced rung after a handful of clients instead of after a few years of quiet erosion
pros.example: noticing that every client with inventory overran its effort estimate and moving inventory up a rung before the next quarter of selling

cons.claim: The loop depends on delivery measurement that a small practice often fails to keep, so its inputs are weakest exactly when the practice is busiest
cons.example: a review quarter with no effort data at all because everyone was closing books instead of recording their time

failure_modes: running the loop only after one painful client rather than on the schedule
changing fees for new sales while never revisiting the assumption that produced the old ones
treating a single bad engagement as proof that a whole rung is wrong
acceptance_tests: the loop runs on its stated rhythm with all four evidence streams present or explicitly marked missing, and every change it makes names the evidence that produced it
revisit_triggers: an evidence stream goes missing for a whole review cycle
a change made by the loop does not improve the next cohort

base.update_signal: whether the next cohort of sold deals shows that the previous correction actually worked

edges.why_related: the boundary is drawn around the body of work the charter says the subscription covers, so the charter must exist before the line can be placed
what the subscription promises to do each month determines which client systems it must reach and therefore what access design is needed
candidates are compared against the buyer and the recurring promise the charter defines, not against general industry appeal
a workload signature is only built for the short-listed candidates the comparison produced, because building one is expensive
committing to a niche without knowing what one of its months actually contains is a guess dressed as a strategy
the case for committing rests on the compounding channels being real and observable in this niche rather than assumed
the units worth counting are the drivers the signature identified as moving the month, not a generic list of accounting attributes
rungs are cut on band ranges of the scope units, so the units and their verification sources must exist first
a ladder is cut for one niche's shape; the same rungs would land in the wrong places for a different kind of business
exclusions are written per rung, so what each rung includes must be settled before what it excludes can be stated
a trigger describes movement between rungs, which requires the rungs and their band ranges to already exist
the fee is derived per rung from the scope that rung carries, so scope precedes price rather than the reverse
the effort estimate inside the fee mechanism is read off the signature, and the uncertainty premium is sized by how much of it is still hypothesis
the catalogue exists to give the excluded items a priced destination, so the exclusions define what the catalogue must contain
the comparison against hourly billing rests on being able to explain how the fixed fee was actually derived and what risk it transfers
the first screen test asks whether the prospect is inside the committed niche, which presupposes the commitment has been made
condition is only worth reading once the prospect has passed the fit tests, otherwise the practice does unpaid diagnostic work for someone it will decline
the artifact can only contain what the sale captured, so the capture rule must operate before the gate can be meaningful
one whole family of exclusions is fixed by the boundary and cannot be sold at any price or in any rung
the mandatory declines are derived from the boundary, so the refusal sentence and the referral destination come straight from it
the access terms and confidentiality commitment are required contents of the artifact, and no credential may be accepted before it exists
the de-identification rule limits what any sales asset may show, which is why samples are synthetic and references are permissioned
the disclosure order and the no-upsell-under-distress rule constrain how the screen is run so it informs the prospect rather than pressuring them
