every add-on sold is evidence that the rung was cut in the wrong place, yet moving the work into the rung raises the headline fee and slows sales
edges.resolution_rule: when the validation loop shows a majority of clients in the niche buying the same add-on, promote it into the rung and re-derive that rung's fee; below that threshold keep it separate and keep selling it explicitly rather than absorbing it

edges.why_related: the niche filter rejects revenue that is available right now, and the pressure to waive it is strongest in a thin month
edges.resolution_rule: an out-of-niche prospect may only be accepted as a labelled exception on the custom path with no efficiency or price promise; if labelled exceptions exceed the stated exception budget in a review cycle, re-open the niche decision itself rather than relaxing the filter quietly

edges.why_related: every decline removes revenue the practice is trying to grow, so the decline rule and the commercial goal pull in opposite directions
edges.resolution_rule: mandatory declines always win regardless of pipeline; a discretionary decline may be waived only as a written labelled exception naming who approved it and carrying a review date in the first months

edges.why_related: the fixed fee genuinely costs the client more in a quiet month, which is exactly the fact the hourly comparison is tempted to leave out
edges.resolution_rule: disclose the quiet-month case explicitly as part of the comparison; where a prospect's volume is genuinely small and stable, decline toward the hourly alternative rather than winning on an incomplete comparison

edges.why_related: the triage wants evidence out of the books while the access discipline limits what a prospect should hand over before anything is signed
edges.resolution_rule: triage runs on client-produced exports and a time-limited read-only view only; if the prospect cannot supply evidence without handing over shared credentials, record the unknown condition band and quote conditionally or defer rather than accepting the credentials

edges.why_related: reuse of rulesets and the exception library lowers measured cost-to-serve over time, which moves the cost floor the fee is built on
the capture rule is what produces the out-of-scope request register the loop reads; without it the loop has one of its four evidence streams missing
a change in a client's business that is discrete rather than permanent fails the sustained-breach test and is therefore routed to an add-on instead of a rung move
the selling stance produces the manner of the decline, which is why a no is delivered plainly and early and is never converted into a fear pitch
the screen runs before any proposal conversation, so the three-way answer discipline applies to a prospect who has already been qualified in
only engagements that passed the gate carry the recorded scope, counts and fee derivation the loop later compares delivery against
measured overruns and clustered between-rung placements feed back into where the rungs are cut for the next cohort of sales
a unit that turns out not to predict delivery effort is replaced or re-banded, which is a change to the unit dictionary itself
recorded decline reasons accumulate into evidence about which candidate niches actually produce fit prospects and which do not

both are alternative-comparison units built the same way: name the structural difference, illustrate it with the niche's own recurring exception, and concede the cases where the alternative genuinely wins

conflict_axes.name: niche_focus_versus_available_revenue
conflict_axes.description: Committing to one niche is what makes the offer efficient, but every out-of-niche prospect who calls is real money the filter turns away, and the pressure to waive the filter is highest in a thin month.
poles: serve only the committed niche
quote whoever calls
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accept out-of-niche work only as a labelled custom exception with no efficiency promise, and treat a rising exception rate as a reason to re-open the niche decision rather than to abandon the filter

conflict_axes.name: fixed_fee_certainty_versus_estimation_risk
conflict_axes.description: The whole appeal of the subscription is a number the owner can count on, but that number is set before the practice has seen a single month of their books, so certainty for the client is risk for the practice.
poles: give the prospect a firm number now
hold the price until effort is observed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quote firmly inside the rung the verified scope units place them on, carry an uncertainty premium sized by how much of the signature is still hypothesis, and reserve a stated re-quote right where counts could not be verified

conflict_axes.name: ladder_simplicity_versus_scope_precision
conflict_axes.description: A short ladder is easy to sell and easy to explain, while precise bands across many units describe reality better and mis-serve fewer clients at the edges.
poles: few simple rungs
precise bands on many units
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the rung count small and push precision into the scope-unit bands and the add-on catalogue rather than into extra rungs

conflict_axes.name: sales_momentum_versus_qualification_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Prospects want a price in the first conversation, while the screen and the condition triage both have to happen before a price means anything.
poles: give a number on the first call
screen and triage before quoting
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: explain that the number depends on countable facts, ask the counting questions in the same conversation, and give an indicative band with stated assumptions rather than either a firm price or a refusal to speak about money

conflict_axes.name: generosity_versus_precedent
conflict_axes.description: Doing the small extra thing builds the relationship a small-business subscription depends on, and simultaneously sets the precedent that erodes the scope for every client afterwards.
poles: say yes to the small extra
route every request through the three destinations
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route the request, and if the practice chooses to absorb it anyway, label it a dated one-off in writing so it never becomes the unspoken standard

conflict_axes.name: helpfulness_versus_licensed_boundary
conflict_axes.description: The owner asks the bookkeeper the tax and structure questions because the bookkeeper is the person who sees their numbers, and being useful in that moment means crossing into licensed territory.
poles: answer the question the owner actually asked
refuse on the class and refer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer only the bookkeeping-side part - what the records show - and hand the interpretation to a licensed professional using the standing referral sentence, with the request logged

conflict_axes.name: client_convenience_versus_least_privilege_access
conflict_axes.description: Owners offer the fastest access they know, which is usually their own password, and insisting on provisioned least-privilege access costs time at the exact moment the prospect is most enthusiastic.
poles: accept whatever access the owner offers
insist on provisioned least-privilege access
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never accept shared credentials at any stage; keep a prepared provisioning path per platform so the compliant route is also the fast route

conflict_axes.name: competitor_anchoring_versus_measured_cost_to_serve
conflict_axes.description: Prospects arrive quoting numbers they saw advertised, and the fastest way to answer is to price against those numbers instead of against what the work actually costs this practice to deliver.
poles: match the number the prospect saw
hold the fee the mechanism produced
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat any external figure as an unverified claim, re-derive from measured cost-to-serve, and if the gap cannot be closed honestly, decline rather than sell below the floor

conflict_axes.name: persuasive_proof_versus_client_confidentiality
conflict_axes.description: The most persuasive proof would be a real client's real numbers, and that is precisely the material the practice is trusted never to show.
poles: show real client work
show only synthetic and permissioned material
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build every sample on labelled synthetic figures, seek written permission for any named reference, and never let a persuasion need override the confidentiality commitment

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_start_versus_written_engagement
conflict_axes.description: An enthusiastic owner wants work to begin immediately, while the engagement gate insists that nothing starts and no credential is accepted until the scope, fee, triggers and access terms exist in writing.
poles: start now on a verbal agreement
no artifact, no first month
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the artifact short enough to issue the same day and hold the gate absolutely; speed comes from a fast artifact, never from skipping it

edge_cases.description: A single-site restaurant has started selling branded goods through an online marketplace, so two completely different workload signatures now run inside one client
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect's business spans two niches at once
edge_cases.mitigation: count the second channel as its own scope unit and place the client on the rung that carries both, or quote a labelled custom scope; never average the two signatures into an optimistic middle

edge_cases.description: A prospect wants the subscription to include their annual tax return and to handle a letter they received from a tax authority
edge_cases.trigger: the prospect's stated need crosses into licensed-professional territory
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse on the class using the standing sentence, refer to a licensed professional, and offer only the bookkeeping-side support of supplying clean records to whoever the client engages

edge_cases.description: A prospect insists on a firm monthly price before granting any access or producing a single statement
edge_cases.trigger: price is demanded before any scope unit can be verified
edge_cases.mitigation: give an indicative band tied to explicitly stated assumptions plus a written right to re-quote once counts are verified, and never let an indicative band become a signed fee without that verification

edge_cases.description: The books are so far behind that no period can be closed and no balance agrees to a statement
edge_cases.trigger: the condition triage returns materially behind
edge_cases.mitigation: scope and price the catch-up as its own project under the onboarding KB and begin the subscription only from the first period that can actually be closed

edge_cases.description: A landscaping client crosses the transaction volume band only during its summer peak and sits well below it for the rest of the year
edge_cases.trigger: a seasonal business trips a volume trigger it does not structurally exceed
edge_cases.mitigation: define the trigger as a sustained breach across consecutive months with a seasonal averaging rule agreed at the sale, and pair it with a downward trigger

edge_cases.description: The marketplace most of the niche sells on changes its payout report format, so the recurring monthly exception changes shape for every client at once
edge_cases.trigger: a dominant platform in the committed niche changes its reporting
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a signature change, re-derive the effort estimate for new sales immediately, and hand the consequence for existing clients to the practice-economics KB rather than silently absorbing it

edge_cases.description: An owner arrives frightened, with a lender deadline days away and no idea what their numbers say
edge_cases.trigger: distress signals appear during the first conversation
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the conversation down, write the options in plain language, offer no higher tier while the distress is present, and name the licensed professional they may need before they need a bookkeeper

edge_cases.description: A prospect sends their online banking username and password by message before anyone has asked for anything
edge_cases.trigger: unsolicited credential sharing during the sale
edge_cases.mitigation: do not use the credentials, tell the prospect to change them, send the least-privilege provisioning path instead, and record the event as an access near-miss

edge_cases.description: A prospect asks for personal spending to be booked as business expense, or for revenue to be held back into a later period, as a condition of signing
edge_cases.trigger: a request that would misstate the books arrives during the sale
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a mandatory decline, state plainly that the records must reflect what happened, refer the underlying question to a licensed professional, and record the reason

edge_cases.description: A referring accountant has already told the prospect a scope and a price that do not match any rung
edge_cases.trigger: a referral arrives with expectations pre-set by a third party
edge_cases.mitigation: reset expectations in writing against the band table and exclusion list before quoting, and where the referrer's promise cannot be met inside a rung, quote the custom path or decline rather than discounting quietly to protect the relationship

edge_cases.description: A sole trader with one account, a handful of transactions a month and no employees asks to buy the lowest rung
edge_cases.trigger: a prospect who does not need the product wants to buy it
edge_cases.mitigation: disqualify honestly, explain that their software plus an annual visit to a professional is the better fit, and record the decline reason rather than taking easy revenue

edge_cases.description: A small monthly favour agreed during the sale to close the deal has quietly become a standing expectation the fee never covered
edge_cases.trigger: an unlabelled concession hardens into standard scope
edge_cases.mitigation: name it in the validation loop, route it to the add-on catalogue or promote it into the rung for future sales, and hand the conversation with the existing client to the practice-economics KB

workflow.description: State the buyer, the recurring body of work, the rhythm class and the three refusals before anything else is designed
workflow.gate: a person outside the practice can use the charter to judge whether a named request is inside or outside the subscription

workflow.description: Classify every service line as bookkeeping-side or licensed-side and write the refusal and referral sentence for each licensed-side item
workflow.artifact: boundary card with refusal and referral sentences
workflow.gate: no service line is unclassified and no marketing or proposal text asserts a jurisdiction-specific rule or designation without local verification

workflow.description: Decide the least-privilege access each rung needs, the provisioning path per platform, and the practices that are refused outright
workflow.artifact: per-tier access matrix and prohibited-access list
workflow.gate: every system a rung needs has a named least-privilege provisioning path and the prohibited list is written for use in the sales conversation

workflow.description: Define candidates narrowly and score them on the attributes that decide fixed-fee viability, recording the observation behind each score
workflow.artifact: niche comparison sheet with a short list
workflow.gate: each candidate is defined narrowly enough for consistent classification and no score rests on an unattributed market figure

workflow.action: Build the workload signature for each short-listed niche
workflow.description: Describe one month of that niche's bookkeeping including money-in, money-out, feeds, documents, judgment classes, seasonality and the recurring exception
workflow.artifact: workload signature worksheet per short-listed niche
workflow.gate: every element of every signature is labelled observed or hypothesis and the recurring monthly exception is named

workflow.action: Commit to the niche and cap concentration
workflow.description: Choose one niche, list what changes operationally, set the concentration limit and adjacency plan, and record the reversal conditions
workflow.gate: the memo names one niche, the artifacts that change, a concentration limit, the named shock exposures and the reversal conditions

workflow.description: Fix the units that place a client on a rung, each with a definition, a verification source and band edges, excluding anything unverifiable before the sale
workflow.gate: two people counting the same prospect independently reach the same rung placement

workflow.description: Build the short ladder plus the labelled custom path, answering the four questions for every rung
workflow.gate: adjacent rungs differ by at least one named body of work and every rung states its work, rhythm, bands and client responsibilities

workflow.action: Write the exclusions and route them
workflow.description: Write the four exclusion families in client language, each with its destination, and prepare the add-on entries and upgrade triggers they imply
workflow.artifact: exclusion and routing sheet with the add-on catalogue
workflow.gate: every exclusion is in client language with a named destination and no licensed-professional work appears in the add-on catalogue

workflow.action: Derive the fee for each rung
workflow.description: Build the fee from effort estimate, cost floor, uncertainty premium and value context, and set the per-deal verification check
workflow.gate: each rung's fee traces to the four inputs, the effort estimate is marked observed or estimated, and no external figure appears as an unlabelled fact

workflow.action: Qualify the prospect and read the condition of the books
workflow.description: Run the six tests, take the shallow condition evidence, choose one of the four outcomes and record the reason
workflow.artifact: prospect screen record with condition band
workflow.gate: all six tests are answered, a condition band is supported by named evidence, and the outcome and reason are recorded even when no proposal follows

workflow.action: Issue the engagement artifact and open the validation loop
workflow.description: Put scope, counts, exclusions, fee, triggers, catch-up path, access terms, client responsibilities, boundary statement and exit terms in writing, then register the deal for later comparison against delivery
workflow.artifact: signed engagement artifact and validation register entry
workflow.gate: no element is missing, the template has had local professional review, and no work or credential is accepted before it is in place

dominance_rules.rule: The licensed-work boundary dominates every scope, pricing and revenue decision
dominance_rules.rationale: crossing into attest, tax or legal territory exposes the practice and the client to consequences no subscription fee can justify, and the rules differ by jurisdiction
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect or client asks for work whose class sits on the licensed side of the boundary
dominance_rules.action: refuse on the class using the standing sentence, refer to a licensed professional, log the request, and never price the work as an add-on

dominance_rules.rule: Client data confidentiality and least-privilege access dominate sales convenience and speed
dominance_rules.rationale: the practice is trusted with the most sensitive data a small business holds, and one careless access shortcut can end the practice
dominance_rules.trigger: any moment where accepting shared credentials, a personal-device workaround or real client data in a sample would be faster
dominance_rules.action: refuse the shortcut, use the provisioned path, and use synthetic or permissioned material in every sales asset

dominance_rules.rule: Written scope dominates anything that was said out loud
dominance_rules.rationale: memory of a sales conversation diverges immediately and the client's memory is the one that will govern the relationship
dominance_rules.trigger: delivery or the client believes something was promised that the proposal does not contain
dominance_rules.action: treat it as out of scope, route it to add-on or referral, and if the practice chooses to honour it, record it as a dated one-off

dominance_rules.rationale: a mis-fit client costs more than the revenue it brings and consumes the capacity a fit client would have used
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect fails a mandatory decline condition or is plainly better served elsewhere while the pipeline is thin
dominance_rules.action: decline plainly, name the alternative, record the reason, and do not soften the decline into a smaller sale

dominance_rules.rationale: an advertised price elsewhere carries no information about this practice's scope, quality or overhead and is an unverified claim
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect presents a competitor figure or an article's benchmark and asks the practice to match it
dominance_rules.action: label the figure unverified, re-state the derivation, and decline the deal rather than price below the measured floor

dominance_rules.rule: The niche workload signature dominates the owner's self-reported volume
dominance_rules.rationale: owners systematically under-report accounts, channels and the mess, while the signature is built from observation
dominance_rules.trigger: what the prospect describes conflicts with what the signature and their own documents show
dominance_rules.action: price from the verified counts and the signature, and state the assumption gap in the proposal

dominance_rules.rule: The condition band dominates the subscription start date
dominance_rules.rationale: a subscription that silently absorbs a catch-up project is mispriced from month one and poisons the relationship it is meant to start
dominance_rules.trigger: the triage returns materially behind or unknown
dominance_rules.action: agree a separately scoped and separately priced catch-up first, and start the monthly fee from the first closable period

dominance_rules.rule: Fear-free framing dominates urgency, especially with a distressed owner
dominance_rules.rationale: selling on fear produces clients who resent the purchase, and speculating about what an authority might do also crosses the licensed boundary
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect is frightened, behind, or under a third-party deadline
dominance_rules.action: slow down, disclose in plain language, offer no higher tier while distress is present, and refer where their real need is licensed work

dominance_rules.rule: Ladder integrity dominates any single deal
dominance_rules.rationale: a bespoke rung invented for one prospect becomes the precedent that unpicks the whole ladder for everyone who follows
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect can only be won by inventing a new rung or quietly bending a band
dominance_rules.action: quote the labelled custom path or decline, and take the pattern to the validation loop instead of changing the ladder for one deal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Draw the licensed-work boundary before writing any rung scope
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tiers that promise work the practice must later retract, and marketing that has to be rewritten after a professional review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the niche workload signature before deriving any fee
anti_rework_rules.prevents: fee levels that have to be renegotiated in month three, and an uncertainty premium nobody knew they needed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define countable scope units before cutting the ladder
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rungs separated by adjectives that no one can adjudicate and that have to be re-cut once real prospects arrive

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the exclusion list in the same sitting as the inclusion list
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every out-of-scope request becoming an individual negotiation, and exclusions being discovered by clients inside the engagement artifact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the upgrade and downgrade triggers before the first client crosses one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a repricing conversation that the client experiences as a penalty, and a ladder that decays because nobody dares move anyone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Commit to the niche before building positioning language and proof assets
anti_rework_rules.prevents: generic proof that persuades nobody and has to be rebuilt from scratch once the niche is chosen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Triage the condition of the books before quoting any monthly fee
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a subscription price that silently absorbs a catch-up project and cannot be corrected without renegotiating a new relationship

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the access provisioning path per platform before any engagement is signed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: credential-sharing improvisation in week one and an access clean-up that is impossible to fully undo

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record every prospect outcome and decline reason at the moment it happens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rediscovering the same mis-fit pattern deal after deal because the evidence was never captured while it was cheap

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured delivery effort diverges from the rung's effort estimate for two or more consecutive months across more than one client
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the fee mechanism inputs and re-cut the affected band edges for new sales, and hand the existing-client consequence to the practice-economics KB

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same out-of-scope request arrives from several clients in the niche
iteration_protocol.action: decide explicitly whether it becomes a catalogue add-on or is promoted into the rung, and rewrite the exclusion list either way

iteration_protocol.trigger: a platform or source system central to the niche changes its payouts, statements or exports
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the affected part of the workload signature, re-derive the effort estimate, and check whether any trigger definition has become uncountable

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same objection decides several losses in a row
iteration_protocol.action: rework the comparison that fails, checking that it concedes honestly where the alternative wins, and refresh the proof asset it depends on

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client who passed the screen turns out to be a mis-fit within the first months
iteration_protocol.action: identify which screen test or condition question failed to catch it and rewrite that test before the next quote goes out

iteration_protocol.trigger: regulator or professional-body guidance changes, or the same request keeps landing ambiguously on the boundary
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the obligation classes locally with a qualified professional, restate the refusal sentences, and update the engagement template

iteration_protocol.trigger: niche concentration passes the stated limit or a named shock hits the chosen niche
iteration_protocol.action: re-score the adjacent candidates and decide whether to open an adjacency, without abandoning the committed niche on a single bad quarter

iteration_protocol.trigger: an access near-miss, an incident, or a platform access-model change occurs
iteration_protocol.action: revise the per-tier access matrix and provisioning paths, re-check every sales asset for identifiable client material, and update the engagement terms

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the charter, the licensed-work boundary, the access design and the selling stance decide what may be sold at all; niche work follows because the workload signature is the evidence every band and fee later rests on; offer design (scope units, ladder, exclusions, triggers, fee, add-ons) can only be cut once that evidence exists; positioning and proof are built for the committed niche and the finished ladder; qualification, triage, decline and sale-stage scope discipline apply the finished offer to one prospect at a time; and the engagement gate and validation loop come last because they close the offer over real deals and feed every correction back into the nodes above.
